newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico says to reimburse Telmex for costs.
newsitem.headline: Mexico says to reimburse Telmex for costs.

text.p: Mexico's Federal Telecommunications Commission (Cofetel) said on Monday that it would go ahead with plans to reimburse Telmex for costs incurred in interconnecting lines to Telmex's network, despite opposition from competing phone companies.
"(Cofetel) notified on Monday the concessionaires Alestra, Miditel, Telmex and Telnor of the inappropriateness of their requested suspension," the commission said in a statement.

Cofetel president Carlos Casasus has said that Telmex would be awarded $422 million for its investment in sharing its phone lines wih rivals, a government requirement for the end of Telmex's monopoly over long-distance service.
The reimbursement would be paid by the holders of the long distance service concessions, he said.

Legal complaints to the reimbursement were registered by long distance competitors such as Alestra, formed of AT&T and Grupo Financiero Banamex-Accival, and Avantel, a venture between MCI Corp, Mexico's Alfa and holding company VISA-Bancomer.
